referenceReview.boundary: PlayFlow, Nakama, Firebase, and Supabase remain reference-only, with no reference API, source, dependency, or wire contract copied. Agones is no longer reference-only: its client loop shape (sdks/csharp/sdk/AgonesSDK.cs and sdks/unity/AgonesSdk.cs at v1.60.0, commit 67b44a783218f7811084adaa5d9b334fb28e44ba) is adopted under Apache-2.0 as a marked modified derivative in Yogabase.Yogabase.RuntimeHost and its Unity package, retargeted to Yogabase's own self-scoped runtime-host routes. No Agones name, proto/sdk wire contract, resource concept, or host-port policy was adopted. The unmodified licence ships at licenses/Apache-2.0-Agones.txt; the full copying boundary is recorded in docs/REFERENCE_REVIEW.md

contract.mirroredFrom: Byte-identical, like the builds, delivery and runtime-host documents below, to the product document at main beb61e56 (2026-10-08); this document last changed in b088fb38 (2026-10-08), the delivery document in ec3c58b5 (2026-10-03), the builds document in 1f7ad8a3 (2026-09-22) and the runtime-host document in 87469584 (2026-09-17), and all four were compared byte for byte with the product's files at beb61e56. It carries the player-facing /v1/servers/* game-server surface, the three external sign-in routes for a project's end users (/auth/external/{provider}/start, /return and /callback, db336487, 73b01e6f and b088fb38, 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08; the callback now requires the codeVerifier whose challenge start received), the requested-only realtime-presence and data-rest capability rows with the X-Yogabase-Accept-Capabilities request header, the restored client Data API (/v1/data/{table}/select|insert|upsert|update|delete, 9f14ca68, 2026-09-23) with its named 413 data_request_too_large (360a31c1), the storage refusal codes (858071ba, 2026-09-24), the inline payload limit with the 413 payload_too_large refusal on the function invoke route (9f653644, 2026-10-03) and on the actor invoke, workflow start and workflow cancel routes at 480 KiB (x-yogabase-orleans-payload, b1d8c286), the durable Jobs routes (/v1/projects/{projectId}/jobs, 1b925cc0, 2026-10-03, x-yogabase-jobs) and the schedule routes (/v1/projects/{projectId}/schedules/{scheduleId} and its /trigger, 552fdb4f, 2026-10-03, x-yogabase-schedules), which three later product commits of the same day tightened: a manual run of a schedule whose function version is no longer admitted is a 409 where it was a 503, and both policies are required (195b9845); a write holds scheduleId to one rule, the pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._~:-]{0,127}$ (15ecb4ce); and the concurrency policies state what the scheduler does about an earlier occurrence that has not finished (a95d2347). Kiota therefore generates request builders for the Jobs and schedule routes in TypeScript, Python, Java and Dart, and the authored Jobs and schedule clients sit beside them (jobsSurface and schedulesSurface below).

schedulesSurface.declaredBy: x-yogabase-schedules in contracts/yogabase-client-v1.openapi.json (product commit 552fdb4f, 2026-10-03; the routes had been served and acceptance-tested before the document described them; three later commits the same day, 195b9845, 15ecb4ce and a95d2347, tightened it, and the mirrored document is the one at main f9d57e29); Kiota generates the request builders and models (Schedule, ScheduleDefinitionRequest, ScheduleTriggerRequest, ScheduleTriggerResult, MisfirePolicy, ConcurrencyPolicy) for TypeScript, Python, Java and Dart.
schedulesSurface.authoredFrom: Yogabase product repository at main 92ac1ced: src/Yogabase.Tasks/AppPlatform/Gateway/Functions/ScheduledLambdaGateway.cs, src/Yogabase.Core/Lambda/LambdaScheduleConsoleContracts.cs, tests/Yogabase.AppPlatform.Tests/YogabaseClientSchedulesContractTests.cs, docs/CLIENT_SDKS.md and docs/DEVELOPER_WORKFLOW.md. The schedule id rule, the policy descriptions and the 409 of a manual run of a withdrawn function version were taken from the mirrored contract at main f9d57e29 alone, not from the gateway's source.
schedulesSurface.preconditions: A create sends If-None-Match: * (201), an update sends If-Match with the ETag last read (200), and a delete (204) and a manual run (POST .../trigger, 202) send If-Match; a stale or unmet precondition is 412, a missing one 428, and both at once or a malformed ETag 400.
schedulesSurface.eTag: "schedule-v<version>-<instance as 32 lowercase hex>"; the version is decimal text, a 64-bit number a JSON number cannot carry, that the scheduler also advances as it runs, so an ETag held for long is stale. Every client reads it from the response header and checks it against the body, except Dart, whose typed send cannot read headers and derives it from the body.
schedulesSurface.namedRefusal: 413 schedule_payload_too_large (limitBytes 1,048,576 and maxBodyBytes 8,394,167); every other refusal is a status with a fixed title and no code, or no body, which the clients name by status (precondition_failed, precondition_required, not_found, conflict, forbidden, unsupported_media_type, request_failed).
schedulesSurface.knownGatewayLimits: None is recorded against the contract at product main f9d57e29. A product build from before the three commits of 2026-10-03 behaves as the earlier contract said: the scheduler stores concurrencyPolicy but starts every occurrence whichever is chosen, a manual run of a schedule whose function version is no longer admitted answers 503, a schedule id that contains a slash cannot be written (400) and any other id of 1 to 128 trimmed characters is accepted. The clients follow the later contract; the end-to-end evidence below was taken against the earlier build and was not repeated against f9d57e29.

buildsContract.notGeneratedReason: A developer-tool surface (Unity Editor, CLI, CI) reached with a project-scoped ybt_ developer token, not a shipped-client surface. The .NET YogabaseBuildsClient and the Unity package implement it by hand, including the Lambda execution declaration and registeredLambdaIds; no other language needs a client for it yet, so none is generated.

runtimeHostContract.notGeneratedReason: The document declares instance-addressed paths (/instances/{instanceId}/...), but a hosted workload calls the self-scoped relay routes /runtime-host/v1/self/{heartbeat,ready,reserve,shutdown,assignments} and never learns or asserts its own instance id. Generating from this document would emit the wrong surface for a workload, so it is checked in and checksum-verified as the server-side reference for lifecycle states and error codes only; the workload module is hand-authored.
